# 2 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** In the year one hundred forty-nine, it was reported to Judas and his men that Antiochus Eupator was coming with a great multitude against Judea,

**13:2** and with him Lysias, his guardian, who was over the affairs of state, each of them having a Greek force of one hundred ten thousand infantry, five thousand three hundred cavalry, twenty-two elephants, and three hundred chariots armed with scythes.

**13:3** Menelaus also joined them and with much hypocrisy urged Antiochus on, not for the salvation of his country but because he thought that he would be established in office.

**13:4** But the King of kings roused the passion of Antiochus against this criminal. And when Lysias disclosed that he was the cause of all the troubles, he ordered that he should be brought to Beroea and killed there according to the method practiced in that place.

**13:5** For there is a tower at that place of fifty cubits height, full of ashes, and it has a rim running round it that on all sides inclines precipitously into the ashes.

**13:6** There they all push anyone guilty of sacrilege or notorious for any other crimes to his destruction.

**13:7** By such a fate it happened that Menelaus the lawbreaker met his end, without even getting a burial in the earth;

**13:8** and indeed quite justly, for since he had committed many sins against the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, in ashes he received his death.

**13:9** The king came on with his mind thoroughly savage and intent to inflict on the Jews things far worse than had been done in his father's time.

**13:10** But when Judas heard of this, he gave orders to the people to call upon the Lord day and night, now if ever to help those who were on the point of being deprived of the law and their fatherland and the holy temple,

**13:11** and not to let the people who had just now begun to revive fall into the hands of the blasphemous Gentiles.

**13:12** So when all together they had done this, beseeching the merciful Lord with weeping and fasting and lying prostrate on their faces for three days without ceasing, Judas exhorted them and commanded them to stand by.

**13:13** And having conferred privately with the elders, he resolved to march out and decide the matter by the help of God before the king's army could enter Judea and take possession of the city.

**13:14** So entrusting the decision to the Creator of the world, and exhorting his men to fight nobly to the death for the laws, the temple, the city, the fatherland, and the way of life, he made his camp near Modein.

**13:15** And having given his men the watchword "God's victory," he led with the very choicest young men he had and made a night attack on the king's pavilion and killed as many as two thousand men in the camp, and stabbed the leading elephant along with the man upon it.

**13:16** And in the end they filled the camp with terror and confusion and withdrew having triumphed.

**13:17** Now this was accomplished as dawn was just breaking, because the protection of the Lord had aided him.

**13:18** The king, having now had a taste of the daring of the Jews, attempted to take the positions by stratagem.

**13:19** And he marched against Beth-zur, a strong fortress of the Jews, but was turned back, failed, and lost men.

**13:20** Maccabeus sent to those inside whatever was needed.

**13:21** But Rhodocus, someone from the Jewish ranks, disclosed secret information to the enemy. He was sought out and arrested and put in prison.

**13:22** The king negotiated again with those in Beth-zur, gave his hand in pledge, received theirs, and departed.

**13:23** He attacked Judas and was repulsed. And he got word that Philip, who had been left in charge of the government at Antioch, had revolted. He was dismayed, and on terms he withdrew, agreeing with the Jews to observe all just conditions, swore, and departed. And having sacrificed to the Lord and honored the temple, he departed, generously treating Maccabeus.

**13:24** He received Hegemonides as governor from Ptolemais to Gerar.

**13:25** And he went to Ptolemais; the people of Ptolemais were displeased about the treaty, for they were angry and wanted to annul its terms.

**13:26** Lysias mounted the public platform and gave the best defense possible, persuaded them, mollified them, gained their goodwill, and returned to Antioch. This is how the attack and withdrawal of the king turned out.
